stemMd: Which event is an example of substrate-level phosphorylation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Direct transfer of a phosphate group from an organic intermediate to ADP

options.label: B
options.textMd: ATP synthesis driven by proton flow through a membrane enzyme

options.label: C
options.textMd: Diffusion of oxygen into a cell

explanationMd: Substrate-level phosphorylation forms ATP by direct phosphate transfer from a phosphorylated substrate. It differs from chemiosmotic ATP synthesis, which uses a membrane gradient.

distractorRationale.d: This consumes rather than forms ATP.
distractorRationale.e: DNA copying is not the ATP-forming event described.
distractorRationale.c: This transfers no phosphate to ADP.
